title: Runtime: what happens on a request
lede: Three paths: A, Muse acts for Sam. B, Meta’s Muse asks through the Airline Connector. C, Sam signs in as himself with no agent and is denied.

lanes.label: A. Muse in this demo, real mode: the agent acts for Sam
B. Through the Airline Connector: Meta's Muse asks Muse
C. Just a user, no agent: Sam signs in as himself

nodes.label: 1. Sam asks
sub: "Show my airline points"

nodes.label: 2. Muse calls the gateway
sub: no token on purpose: 401 + where to sign in

nodes.label: 3. PingOne sign-in
sub: DaVinci: password, Protect, MFA on medium risk

nodes.label: 4. Agent detected
sub: Muse turns RED if Protect flagged it, BLUE if only the client id did

nodes.label: 5. Sam consents
sub: Muse Consent screen

nodes.label: 6. Code back to Muse
sub: swapped for Sam's token, kept on the server

nodes.label: 7. Muse acts for Sam
sub: agent token + 2 token exchanges: sub = Sam, act = Muse

nodes.label: 8. Muse asks again
sub: with the delegated token

nodes.label: 9. PingOne Authorize
sub: audience, actor and tool checked

nodes.label: 10. Tool runs
sub: 4,500 points, Gold

nodes.label: 1. User asks in Meta's Muse
sub: "How many United points do I have?"

nodes.label: 2. Meta's Muse picks the connector
sub: reads tool names and descriptions; the airline name in them decides

nodes.label: 3. /mcp answers 401
sub: with metadata: sign in at Muse's own authorize endpoint

nodes.label: 4. PingOne sign-in
sub: same DaVinci flow; login hint ends .conn

nodes.label: 5. Airline Connector Consent
sub: PingOne screen names the connector

nodes.label: 6. Muse does the exchanges
sub: same agent token + 2 exchanges as part A

nodes.label: 7. Muse gives Meta its own token
sub: the PingOne token never leaves Muse

nodes.label: 8. Meta calls /mcp with it
sub: Muse calls the gateway for it

nodes.label: 9. Answer comes back
sub: points and tier, shown in Meta's Muse

nodes.label: 1. Sign in as Sam (no agent)
sub: button on Muse

nodes.label: 2. PingOne sign-in
sub: the Muse user login app: no agent screen, no consent

nodes.label: 3. Sam's own token
sub: no act claim, nothing exchanged

nodes.label: 4. Straight to the gateway
sub: DENIED: no agent acting for him

steps.title: Ask
steps.what: Sam asks Muse: "Show my airline points".
steps.why: Muse acts only when asked.

steps.title: 401, sign in
steps.what: Muse calls the gateway with no token, on purpose. The 401 says where to sign in.
steps.why: Nothing authenticated has been sent yet.

steps.title: Protect check
steps.what: PingOne runs the DaVinci flow: password, Protect risk, MFA on medium risk. Protect also checks whether the app is an agent.
steps.why: The agent is recognised by PingOne, not by its own word.

steps.title: Agent screen
steps.what: Sam sees "AI agent detected". The agent name is red if Protect flagged it, blue if only the client id did.
steps.why: Sam knows an agent is asking before he consents.

steps.title: Consent
steps.what: Sam allows Muse to act for him. PingOne returns a code to Muse.
steps.why: Consent is recorded before any token is issued.

steps.title: Code to token
steps.what: Muse swaps the code for Sam’s token. It stays on the Muse server.
steps.why: The browser never sees a token.

steps.title: Delegation
steps.what: Muse gets its own agent token, then makes two token exchanges. The result has sub = Sam and act = Muse.
steps.why: The gateway can tell who acts for whom.

steps.title: Authorize check
steps.what: Muse asks again with the delegated token. The gateway checks it, then asks PingOne Authorize: right audience, Muse a registered actor, tool allowed.
steps.why: Policy decides every tool call.

steps.title: Tool runs
steps.what: Allowed, so the tool runs and returns 4,500 points, Gold.
steps.why: The answer exists only because every check passed.

steps.title: Ask
steps.what: The user asks in Meta’s Muse: "How many United points do I have?"
steps.why: The user never leaves Meta’s Muse.

steps.title: Picks connector
steps.what: Meta’s Muse reads each connector’s tool names and descriptions and picks the one for the airline.
steps.why: The airline name in the descriptions tells two airline connectors apart.

steps.title: 401, sign in
steps.what: /mcp answers 401 with metadata pointing at Muse’s own authorize endpoint. Meta’s Muse sends the user to PingOne.
steps.why: Standard MCP OAuth discovery.

steps.title: Sign-in
steps.what: The same DaVinci flow runs. The login hint ends .conn, so its screens name the Airline Connector.
steps.why: Sam sees which connector is asking.

steps.title: Consent
steps.what: Sam allows the Airline Connector. PingOne returns a code to Muse.
steps.why: Consent names the connector, not just Muse.

steps.title: Exchanges
steps.what: Muse does the agent token and the two exchanges, as in path A.
steps.why: Authorize treats a connector call like any agent call.

steps.title: Muse token
steps.what: Muse gives Meta’s Muse its own token. The PingOne token never leaves Muse.
steps.why: Meta never holds a PingOne token.

steps.title: Answer
steps.what: Meta’s Muse calls /mcp. Muse calls the gateway with the delegated token and returns the points and tier.
steps.why: The answer comes back through the same checks as path A.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.what: Sam clicks "Sign in as Sam (no agent)".
steps.why: A human login, shown next to the agent login.

steps.title: Own token
steps.what: The Muse user login app is not the Muse app, so there is no agent screen and no consent. PingOne issues Sam’s own token.
steps.why: The flow decides by app id.

steps.title: Denied
steps.what: Muse sends Sam’s own token straight to the gateway. No act claim and the wrong audience: 401.
steps.why: Only a token that names an agent acting for Sam gets through.
